claim: Ruff's E101 only flags a line whose own leading whitespace contains both a tab and a space. pycodestyle flags a line whose indentation character differs from the file's indent character (taken from the first indented line, switched after each report). So a valid Python 3 file that indents one block with tabs and another with spaces gets E101 from pycodestyle and nothing from ruff. A tab-indented project that ignores W191 gets no warning at all for a stray space-indented block.
reference_output: pycodestyle 2.15.0: 6:1 E101 indentation contains mixed spaces and tabs | flake8 7.4.1: 6:1 E101 indentation contains mixed spaces and tabs
ruff_output: (none) [with --select E101,W191 only 2:1 W191 Indentation contains tabs; same with --preview]
evidence:
pycodestyle.py tabs_or_spaces: `for offset, char in enumerate(indent): if char != indent_char: return offset, "E101 ..."` (indent_char is set by readline from the first line starting with whitespace and reset after each E101 in check_physical). pycodestyle testing/data/E10.py, first case (valid Py3: `if True:
	pass` followed by space-indented code), expects "E101 E122 W191 W191". ruff main mixed_spaces_and_tabs.rs: `if indent.contains(' ') && indent.contains('	')`, a per-line check. ruff's own doc example `if a == 0:
        a = 1
	b = 1` mixes across lines, which this check cannot flag. `ruff rule E101` states no deviation. PR #2038 (the original port) does not discuss indent_char. Tracker: #7906 and #8443 (string content) and #18972 (the doc example is a syntax error) only. All commits since 2023 are refactors.
note: Risk: ruff's fixture E101.py labels `def func_tabs():` (space-indented comment, tab-indented body) "# No error", which pycodestyle would flag, so a maintainer may say the per-line semantics are intended. Lead with the doc-example argument. flake8 never resets indent_char (it reports every line that differs from the first indented line), while pycodestyle reports at each transition. Do NOT include the ~4,850 fonttools reports: there pycodestyle takes indent_char from tab-indented string content, which is a pycodestyle quirk. Second repro: a tab-indented function followed by a space-indented one with W191 off gives pycodestyle 7:1 E101 and nothing from ruff.

claim: nested_if_body applies the "nested if must be the only child" test (`body.len() > 1`) to the first `if` branch's body even when the candidate is the last `elif`. So `elif c:` whose body is a lone `if d:` is not reported whenever the first `if` branch holds more than one statement. With a single statement in the first branch, ruff reports it.
reference_output: flake8-simplify 0.31.1: 5:5 SIM102 Use a single if-statement instead of nested if-statements | 13:5 SIM102 Use a single if-statement instead of nested if-statements
ruff_output: 13:5 SIM102 Use a single `if` statement instead of nested `if` statements (same with --preview)
evidence: ruff main collapsible_if.rs nested_if_body: picks `NestedIf::Elif(clause)` from `elif_else_clauses.last()`, then `if body.len() > 1 { return None; }` where `body` is destructured from stmt_if, i.e. the first branch. flake8_simplify rules/ast_if.py get_sim102 runs on the elif's own ast.If node, with the comment "if a: < irrelevant for here". All elif cases in ruff's fixture SIM102.py have a single `pass` in the first branch. Tracker: no match (#23896 and #27647 concern the fix and the default set; #6072 is about indented elif). No main commit touches the check.
note: False negative only: find_last_nested_if still requires the elif body to be a single `if`, so the fix (test nested_if.body() instead of stmt_if.body) adds no false positives. 91 flake8-only reports were on `elif` lines.

claim: redefined_argument_from_local reports a for/with/except target only when the binding it immediately shadows is the parameter (`shadowed.kind.is_argument()`). Every later redefinition of the same parameter is missed: sequential loops, with-targets or except-targets over the same name (on pylint's own functional test ruff gives 3 of the 7 expected reports), and an else-branch loop after an if-branch loop, where the parameter is still intact on that path.
reference_output: pylint 4.1.3: 2:8 R1704 Redefining argument with the local name 'name' | 4:8 R1704 (name) | 10:12 R1704 (x) | 13:12 R1704 (x)
ruff_output: 2:9 PLR1704 Redefining argument with the local name `name` | 10:13 PLR1704 Redefining argument with the local name `x` (same with --preview)
evidence: ruff main redefined_argument_from_local.rs: `let shadowed = &checker.semantic().bindings[shadow.shadowed_id()]; if !shadowed.kind.is_argument() { continue; }`. pylint refactoring_checker _check_redefined_argument_from_local matches every for/with/except AssignName against all argument names of the enclosing function. pylint tests/functional/r/redefined/redefined_argument_from_local.py marks lines 6, 8, 12 (three `with ... as name`) and 26, 28, 30 (three `for name in`); ruff reports only 6, 26 and 50 on that file. In PR #8159's review, charliermarsh proposed the shadowing approach as one that would "achieve the same effect"; nobody stated an intent to skip redefinitions. `ruff rule PLR1704` documents no limit. Tracker: #25228 is about plain assignments, which neither tool flags; nothing else matches.
note: Lead with g(): the else-branch loop overwrites a still-intact parameter, so it is missed even under a value-based reading. A maintainer may answer that after a first loop the parameter value is already gone, so cite pylint's functional test for the sequential cases. A conditional reassignment (`if c: x = 1` then `for x in y`) is missed the same way. The 17 ruff-only reports are `async with` targets, which pylint does not check (REF, not a bug).

claim: Ruff reports a line that holds only a form feed (^L) as "blank line contains whitespace", and its safe fix deletes the form feed. pycodestyle strips form feeds before the check, since PEP 8 allows ^L as a page separator.
repro:
import os
 
print(os)
   (  = one form-feed character)
reference_output: pycodestyle 2.15.0 / flake8: (none)
ruff_output: 2:1 W293 [*] Blank line contains whitespace (the --fix --diff removes the ^L; same with --preview)
evidence: pycodestyle trailing_whitespace: "Strip these trailing characters: ... chr(12), form feed, ^L" `physical_line.rstrip('\n\r\x0c')`. ruff trailing_whitespace.rs uses Rust `char::is_whitespace`. In PR #3122 (the W291/W293 port) the maintainers discussed copying pycodestyle's exact whitespace set and chose to keep `is_whitespace`: the checklist item "follow pycodestyle precedent on what constitutes whitespace" was struck through, charliermarsh called the argument "a good argument in favor of keeping it as-is", and the PR was merged as-is. ruff format also drops lone form feeds by design (#8895, Black's allow_form_feeds, closed as not planned). The pycodestyle maintainer discourages ^L (pycodestyle#1211).
note: Form feeds were not singled out in #3122 (that discussion was about U+00A0), but the decision covers the character set, and the formatter removes ^L too. Do not report.

claim: Ruff checks the operands of every comparison whatever the operator, so membership tests (`np.nan in obj`) and ordering comparisons (`x < np.nan`) are reported. pylint limits nan-comparison to ==, !=, is and is not.
repro:
import numpy as np


def f(x, obj):
    a = np.nan in obj
    b = x < np.nan
    c = x == np.nan
    return a, b, c
reference_output: pylint 4.1.3: 7:8 W0177 Comparison 'x == np.nan' should be 'math.isnan(x)' (nan-comparison)
ruff_output: 5:9 PLW0177 Comparing against a NaN value; use `np.isnan` instead | 6:13 PLW0177 (same) | 7:14 PLW0177 (same)
evidence: ruff main expression.rs: `pylint::rules::nan_comparison(checker, &compare.operands)` with no operator filter. pylint comparison_checker.visit_compare calls _check_nan_comparison only `if operator in {"==", "!=", "is", "is not"}`. The ruff doc says "Checks for comparisons against NaN values" without listing operators, and its fixture tests only `==`. Tracker: nothing (#16374 is the match-case extension, #18596 covers exotic literals).
note: Ordering comparisons against NaN are always False, so flagging them is arguably a useful extension. Membership is the arguable part: `in` checks identity first (`np.nan in [np.nan]` is True), and NaN-aware containers make it correct (all 16 real hits are pandas tests of `np.nan in index`), so the isnan advice is wrong there. Yet `float('nan') in [float('nan')]` and `np.nan in np.array([np.nan])` are both False, so maintainers may keep the check. At most a low-priority suggestion to skip in/not in; not a clear bug.

claim: walk_stmt only descends into If.body, Try.body, With.body, loop bodies and match cases inside a finally block. A return/break/continue in an elif/else branch, an except handler, a try-else or a loop-else inside finally is never reported; bugbear walks every child node. B012 is in ruff's default rule set.
reference_output: flake8-bugbear 26.9.30: 8:13 B012 return/continue/break inside finally blocks cause exceptions to be silenced. ... | 18:13 B012 (same)
ruff_output: (none) (same with --preview and --target-version py314)
evidence: ruff main jump_statement_in_finally.rs walk_stmt matches `Stmt::If(ast::StmtIf { body, .. }) | Stmt::Try(ast::StmtTry { body, .. }) | Stmt::With(ast::StmtWith { body, .. })` plus loop `body` and match cases, and never reads elif_else_clauses, handlers or orelse. bugbear check_for_b012 `_loop` recurses with `ast.iter_child_nodes` (it stops only at nested function defs). CPython 3.14 (PEP 765) emits SyntaxWarning "'return' in a 'finally' block" for all 6 returns of the extended repro (b012_a.py: else, elif, except, nested finally, for-else, try-else); ruff reports 1 of 6 and bugbear all 6. The ruff doc ("Checks for break, continue, and return statements in finally blocks") states no limit. Tracker: none; #20196 asks ruff to cover CPython SyntaxWarnings and names B012, but does not mention this gap.
note: Fix: also walk elif_else_clauses bodies, try handlers, orelse and finalbody, and loop orelse (only `return` for loops, as now). The 9 real flake8-only reports were multiprocess `elif ...: return` (x8) and prompt_toolkit `except Full: ... return`.

claim: import_shadowed_by_loop_var skips unless the import and the loop are in the *same* branch (`!same_branch`). So a loop variable inside an if/try body that the import is not in is never reported, including any function-level loop under an `if` that shadows a module-level import. pyflakes only skips mutually exclusive forks. This is a regression since ruff 0.1.12, and F402 is in the default set.
reference_output: pyflakes 4.0.3 (flake8): 5:9 F402 import 'path' from line 1 shadowed by loop variable | 11:13 F402 import 'path' from line 1 shadowed by loop variable
ruff_output: 5:9 F402 Import `path` from line 1 shadowed by loop variable (same with --preview)
evidence: ruff main pyflakes/rules/imports.rs: the comment says "If the bindings are in different forks, abort." but the code is `.is_none_or(|right| !checker.semantic().same_branch(left, right))`. Commit 985f1d10f (#9418, "Don't flag redefined-while-unused in if branches"; summary and tests cover F811 only) replaced `different_branches` with `!same_branch` at both the F811 and the F402 call sites, and no F402 test changed. ruff 0.1.11 reports 5:9 and 11:13; 0.1.12 and 0.1.13 report only 5:9. pyflakes checker.addBinding reports ImportShadowedByLoopVar unless differentForks (mutually exclusive IF/TRY alternatives). ruff fixture F402.py has no branch case. Tracker: none.
note: All 6 real-world misses have this shape (httplib2 x2, more-itertools, mpmath, litellm, numpy). Example: httplib2 `from email import header`, then `for header in vary_headers:` inside an `if` in a function. The F811 relaxation in #9418 was deliberate; the F402 change was collateral.

claim: undefined_local only looks at each name's latest binding in the function and the binding it directly shadows. A read of a global before a local assignment is therefore missed whenever the function binds the name more than once: two assignments, `x += 1` twice, or an assignment in each branch of an if/else. F823 is in the default set.
repro:
x = 1


def f():
    print(x)
    x = 2


def g():
    print(x)
    x = 2
    x = 3
reference_output: pyflakes 4.0.3 (flake8): 5:11 F823 local variable 'x' defined in enclosing scope on line 1 referenced before assignment | 10:11 F823 (same)
ruff_output: 5:11 F823 Local variable `x` referenced before assignment (same with --preview)
evidence: ruff main pyflakes/rules/undefined_local.rs: `for (name, binding_id) in scope.bindings() { if let Some(shadowed_id) = checker.semantic().shadowed_binding(binding_id) { ... shadowed.references() ... reference.scope_id() == scope_id`. scope.bindings() yields only the latest binding; with two assignments it shadows the first local binding, and the earlier read is a reference of the global, so nothing matches. Also missed: `def g():\n    x += 1\n    x += 1` and `print(x)` followed by an if/else assignment (f823_b.py: pyflakes 5:5, 9:5, 14:11; ruff 5:5). ruff fixture F823.py has only single-assignment cases. Tracker: none (the closed F823 issues are all false positives).
note: Misses a runtime UnboundLocalError. Clean report.

claim: In a chained comparison, ruff checks only the first operand and the right-hand operand of each ==/!=. A None (E711) or True/False (E712) that is the left operand of a later == in the chain is not reported: `a is None == b` means `a is None and None == b`. pycodestyle reports it.
reference_output: pycodestyle 2.15.0: 2:22 E711 comparison to None should be 'if cond is None:' | 6:21 E712 comparison to True should be 'if cond is True:' or 'if cond:'
ruff_output: (none) [ruff reports a lone `None == a` and `a == None == b`]
evidence: ruff main literal_comparisons.rs: the "Check `left`" block handles only compare.first_operand() with compare.first_operator(), and the loop over (op, next) tests only `next.is_none_literal_expr()` and `next` booleans. Ruff maintainers read chains pair by pair (dylwil3 in #24887: "`Date() == [] is None` ... is semantically equivalent to (Date() == []) and ([] is None)"), so `None == b` is a None comparison under ruff's own AST view. pycodestyle's COMPARE_SINGLETON_REGEX matches `None ==`. Tracker: none.
note: The AST view does not explain the gap: ruff flags `None` as the left operand only in the first pair. Real hit: fonttools `userValue is None == xValue is None` (probably meant as XNOR, a latent bug that the warning would expose). Low frequency; a minor item.

claim: EqHash::from_class only reads single-target assignments (`let [Expr::Name(..)] = &targets[..] else { return false; }`). `__eq__` bound by a chained assignment (`__eq__ = __ne__ = op`) or by tuple unpacking is ignored, which is a false negative. `__hash__` bound that way is ignored too, which is a false positive.
reference_output: pylint 4.1.3 (--load-plugins=pylint.extensions.eq_without_hash): 5:0 W1641 Implementing __eq__ without also implementing __hash__ | 9:0 W1641 (same)
ruff_output: 9:7 PLW1641 Object does not implement `__hash__` method | 13:7 PLW1641 Object does not implement `__hash__` method (same with --preview)
evidence: ruff main pylint/rules/eq_without_hash.rs, the ClassMemberKind::Assign arm of EqHash::from_class. The pylint extension uses `set(node.locals)`, which holds every binding. Real hits: dateutil and numpy `__eq__ = __ne__ = ...`. Tracker: none (#14882 was about if-branches and is fixed; #20821 and #18821 are about mutability).
note: `__eq__, __lt__ = op, op` is missed too (class D in plw1641_a.py). The false-positive class F is contrived but has the same root cause; lead with the false negative.

claim: unnecessary_list_index_lookup_comprehension visits only the element expression, not the generator's `if` clauses. It also returns at the first generator that is not an enumerate() instead of continuing. Its dict sibling PLR1733 visits `comp.ifs` and continues.
reference_output: pylint 4.1.3: 2:43 R1736 Unnecessary list index lookup, use 'x' instead | 6:12 R1736 (same)
ruff_output: (no PLR1736) | 10:40 PLR1733 [*] Unnecessary lookup of dictionary value by key (the dict sibling flags the if-clause lookup; same with --preview)
evidence: ruff main unnecessary_list_index_lookup.rs: `let Some((sequence, index_name, value_name)) = enumerate_items(..) else { return; }; ... visitor.visit_expr(elt);`. unnecessary_dict_index_lookup.rs instead uses `else { continue; }` and `visitor.visit_expr(elt); for expr in &comp.ifs { visitor.visit_expr(expr); }`. Tracker: #25182 and the open PR #25233 cover only the for-else and shadowing false positives (#25233 deletes the orelse visit), not comprehensions.

claim: Ruff strips only leading underscores before the CapWords check (`trim_start_matches('_')`); pep8-naming strips both ends (`name.strip('_')`). A CapWords class name with a trailing underscore (`Fine_`, `Password_`) is therefore flagged by ruff only.
repro: class Fine_:\n    pass\n
reference_output: pep8-naming 0.15.1: (none); its testsuite/N801.py marks `class Fine_:`, `class Fine__:` and `class G_:` as Okay
ruff_output: 1:7 N801 Class name `Fine_` should use CapWords convention (same with --preview)

In #15939 MichaReiser wrote "I think this is a deviation on our end ... the upstream rule uses str.strip('_')"; its fix #15988 changed only the leading side. ruff fixture N801.py has no trailing-underscore case. Tracker: nothing else.

claim: The if-expression form is not restricted to known dicts, unlike the statement form since #15995. It fires on non-dict receivers, including `self` inside a dict subclass's own `get`, where the unsafe fix produces `return self.get(key, default)` (infinite recursion). It also fires on custom mappings that have no `.get`.
reference_output: flake8-simplify 0.31.1: (none)
ruff_output: 3:16 SIM401 Use `self.get(key, default)` instead of an `if` block (the --fix --unsafe-fixes diff rewrites the body to `return self.get(key, default)`; same with --preview)

In #15814 MichaReiser wrote: "We've since then started to restrict new rules to known dicts only (e.g. RUF051) and I think it makes sense to do the same here". PR #15995 changed only the statement function. The #15814 example written as a ternary is still flagged (sim401_c.py: 19:10 SIM401 Use `not_dict.get("key", None)`). Tracker: none.

claim: import_from_self only handles `from <parent> import <this module>`. `from <this module> import <name>`, absolute or relative, is never reported, although it is ruff's own doc example and pylint reports it.
repro:
pkg/__init__.py: (empty)
pkg/mod.py: from pkg.mod import foo
from .mod import foo as f2


def foo(): ...
   (run on pkg/mod.py)
reference_output: pylint 4.1.3: 1:0 W0406 Module import itself (import-self) | 2:0 W0406 (same)
ruff_output: (none) [in the same file `import pkg.mod`, `from pkg import mod` and `from . import mod` are reported; same with --preview]
evidence: ruff main pylint/rules/import_self.rs import_from_self compares imported_module_path with `module_path[..module_path.len() - 1]` and looks for an alias equal to the last segment, so the module itself as the source is never matched. The doc example is `# file: this_file.py\nfrom this_file import foo`. Behaviour is identical in 0.0.265, i.e. since the port in #4154. #18972 lists this doc example as not triggering and blames "Relies on specific file name"; that is incomplete, because it fails even with the right module path inside a package.
note: For files outside a package ruff has no module path and reports nothing at all (pylint reports `import other_file` inside other_file.py); that part is probably by design. Mention #18972 in the report.

claim: dict-index-missing-items only checks for statements. Comprehensions and generators (`[ORDERS[k] for k in ORDERS]`) are never checked, though pylint checks them.
reference_output: pylint 4.1.3: 5:4 C0206 Consider iterating with .items() (consider-using-dict-items) | 10:0 C0206 (same)
ruff_output: 5:9 PLC0206 Extracting value from dictionary without calling `.items()` (same with --preview)
evidence: ruff main pylint/rules/dict_index_missing_items.rs: `pub(crate) fn dict_index_missing_items(checker: &Checker, stmt_for: &StmtFor)`, which handles for statements only. pylint recommendation_checker has visit_comprehension / _check_consider_using_dict_items_comprehension, and its functional test consider_using_dict_items.py expects lines 76-84 (dict and list comprehensions, a generator `if`). The ruff doc says "Checks for dictionary iterations ..." with no for-only limit. Tracker: none (#14585 and #13821 are about writes, #14900 about the range).
note: A coverage gap (feature parity) rather than wrong output; frame it as such. Ruff's sibling PLR1733/PLR1736 do have comprehension variants.
